parsed.study_design: Single-utility case study and program evaluation using seismic simulations and public-opinion surveys
parsed.population_and_sample: East Bay Municipal Utility District system and its approximately 1.3 million customers in Alameda and Contra Costa Counties, California; public-opinion survey sample size not reported
parsed.exposure: EBMUD's Seismic Improvement Program, including Board-selected capital investments, seismic design and construction standards, management controls, public participation, and customer-funded financing
parsed.outcome: Modeled post-earthquake water-service availability and restoration, including proportions of customers served and time to minimum or impaired service; customer affordability and support for program funding
parsed.rationale: The Seismic Evaluation section reports Monte Carlo simulations used to compare capital-investment packages according to expected water-system reliability and service goals, with Package 3 selected by the utility's Board (pp. 465–466). Tables 3 and 4 report explicit household-relevant access outcomes, including potable water availability and minimum or impaired service within specified periods and for specified percentages of customers (pp. 471–472). The Public Education and Program Funding sections also report governance and affordability evidence, including ongoing opinion surveys, 91% support, and an estimated typical-customer cost of $1.60 per month (p. 467).
